decisions.muse_failure_discrimination: Dispatch hypothesis tested (06:4x UTC, facilitator run_backend with muse on PATH, cwd the records repo): the decision launch command line is 114 characters because the 7261-character prompt travels in --prompt-file, so the cmd.exe limit does not apply; a tiny prompt with --model default fails ('model `default` does not exist or you lack access'); the same tiny prompt with no --model returns 'pong'. Cause: the model id, not prompt length. 'Agent delegation: auto unavailable: workspace is untrusted' prints in both, inside the repo too, and does not block an answer. On success stdout ('pong') precedes the two 'muse:' stderr lines in run_backend's combined text.

decisions.cycle_4: stopped at the capture (08:08 to 08:12 UTC). Muse's shell call ran as tool_name 'powershell' (tool_batch.effect.started, call_id call_01a1a07599ac710e94fea71ff440b3b7) and failed: 'environment failure: sandbox enforcement unavailable: windows_elevated setup_required: sandbox users are not ready'. The started record carries no command text, so the command field could not be named. Muse's shell sandbox needs an elevated one-time setup on Windows (`muse sandbox windows setup`; `muse sandbox windows check` reads the state); bypass flags (--disable-sandbox, --yolo) exist and are not used. The scope-3 stop rule applies: the cycle ends, Done check 3 stays partly met (probed yes, cited vote yes, scan no-source), and the reader's real shape goes to a follow-up.

notes.muse_not_on_path: Resolved 2026-11-03 about 03:35 UTC: Dispatch appended %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\muse to the user PATH (append only). In a fresh shell `muse` resolves to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\muse\muse.cmd and the live-install case runs and passes (11 tests, no skip).
notes.red2_required_cases: from the facilitator's read of green 1, named in refactor 41ecf78: (a) _detect_sign_in tests 'signed in' before 'not signed in', so a not-signed-in reply reads as signed-in; (b) a version mismatch is appended to problems twice. Criterion 1's cap (1 cycle) is spent, so both go to red 2 (criterion 2 owns the not-signed-in state).
notes.red3_required_cases: green 2's muse backend invocation is 'muse -p {PROMPT} --model {MODEL}', but Muse has no -p flag (`muse --help`): its headless mode is `muse exec`, which has --prompt-file <PATH> (avoids the .CMD shim's 8191-character command-line limit, the cause of the empty Grok and Copilot votes), --session-id <UUID> (pins the session log the reader locates) and --json. The backend is disabled, so nothing misfires now; red 3 must pin a working invocation with {SESSION}.
notes.commit_author: from green 1 (2196c58) on, every Copilot seat commit is authored by the Copilot CLI's own identity ('Copilot', see git log %an); red 1 (5ef4b8f) and red 1b (970118c) carry the shared identity Xipooo. Relevant to card 275 (seat attribution)
notes.gate_gaps: for the gate and the sign-in follow-up: (1) the muse invocation uses --json, so the reply is JSONL events while decider.parse_vote reads a plain first line, so a Muse vote would be voteless until the output is cleaned or --json dropped; (2) --model {MODEL} with models default='default' is unverified against `muse exec`; (3) locate_muse uses only Path.home(), not the slice's XDG_DATA_HOME, then HOME, then USERPROFILE rule; (4) red 3b dropped the disabled and unknown-pin tests. None can be proven before sign-in except (3) and (4).
notes.past_cap_items: after sign-in, items past the D175 caps (each criterion spent its 1 cycle), for a scope window before any red: (1) muse_install._detect_sign_in reports 'unknown' for the signed-in usage text (Tier/Window/Weekly), and Dispatch notes a fresh subscription prints 'No usage data (server_sent_no_usage)', which must read as signed in with unknown quota, never not-signed-in; (2) --json reply versus decider.parse_vote; (3) enabling the muse backend and the card's metric, one Muse voting seat probed, scanned and casting a cited vote in a decision window; (4) locate_muse ignores XDG_DATA_HOME and USERPROFILE; (5) red 3b dropped the disabled and unknown-pin tests; (6) 'Agent delegation: auto unavailable: workspace is untrusted' outside a repo (Dispatch)
notes.muse_plain_output: muse exec without --json prints 'muse: workspace root: <cwd> (cwd default)' and 'muse: Agent delegation: auto unavailable: workspace is untrusted.' before the answer; decider.parse_vote searches for the first sentence-start vote word, so the lines do not void a vote; the facilitator's window runner, which checks a literal first line, must skip them for a Muse seat
notes.model_facts_for_next_window: Dispatch's smoke test `muse exec "Reply with exactly: pong"` used no --model and returned pong; QA's red capture did the same. `muse model-profile show <model>` names catalog ids like muse-spark-1.3 but resolves any string. Options: drop --model (and {MODEL}) from the muse invocation, or pin a catalog id verified by a real call.
notes.bug_placeholder_substitution: facilitator._launch_backend inserts the prompt into the invocation template and then replaces {MODEL} and {SESSION} across the whole string, so placeholder text inside a proposal is rewritten before a seat sees it (QA saw 'sonnet' for '{MODEL}' in window 276-scope-2). To card at close as a bug.
notes.done_check_3_outcome: Done check 3 is partly met. The card cannot be marked Done on the board wording without a product-owner decision: either a waiver like D177 (accept probed + cited vote with a fail-safe no-source scan for this trial, the clean scan moving to a follow-up), or hold the card open until the Windows sandbox setup (an elevated system change only the product owner or Dispatch can make) lets Muse run shell commands, so the reader can be fixed against a real record. Raised to the product owner.
